A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Regression Language Models for Code work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-memory, Triton-latency and neural-architecture prediction experiments, together with ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds GPT-5-Thinking in-context comparisons and Qwen/Llama decoder-only experiments.

M1.justification: The encoder–decoder regressor, explicit numeric tokenization, constrained decoding and autoregressive multi-objective modeling are retained. v2 emphasizes frozen-encoder training, already discussed in v1 Section 6.1; the PDFs do not establish a newly introduced procedure.

E1.justification: The programming-language, APPS/EffiBench, KernelBook and NAS coverage is retained. The new language-model comparisons use existing tasks, including APPS, Amoeba, DARTS and Triton; they introduce different modeling protocols rather than new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-5-Thinking as an in-context comparator in Section 5.1 and Qwen3-0.6B and Llama-3.2-1B as fine-tuned decoder-only comparators in Appendix A.1. These substantially broaden comparison with general language models. Existing graph, embedding and regression-head baselines remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include randomly sampled in-context demonstrations at 0, 3, 5, 20 and approximately 50 shots, with Spearman correlation and prompt-token usage reported. Decoder-only experiments use 1024-token contexts, freeze roughly half the layers and aggregate 128 generated candidates by their parsed median. These are added evaluation designs; retained experiments' stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 adds shot-count and prompt-length sensitivity plus inference-cost analysis. Appendix A.1 investigates decoder-only backbones with ordinary tokenizers and reports malformed numeric outputs. Existing ablations remain, including the pretraining analysis relocated from v1 Section 6.1 to v2 Appendix A.2.

E5.justification: Profiling repeat counts, recorded standard deviations and FLOPs predictive bands are retained. The new comparisons introduce no repeated-training-run reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests. Their generated-candidate counts describe inference aggregation.

E6.justification: New Figure 3 reports GPT-5-Thinking below RLM across four tasks despite generally benefiting from additional demonstrations. Appendix A.1 reports APPS Spearman correlations of approximately 0.17 for Llama and 0.15 for Qwen, versus approximately 0.90 for RLM. These are substantial additional findings; numerical entries in Tables 1–14 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The numeric representation and conditional multi-objective formulations are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions now explicitly state that unified regression works with a frozen encoder and decoder-only training. This refines the central capability claim; the claimed task breadth, headline performance and conclusion remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting ICL limitations to long inputs, finite context, demonstration selection and inference cost. It also attributes decoder-only difficulties to malformed numeric generation and argues for the sample efficiency of specialized numeric outputs. These extend the paper's interpretation beyond its retained graph-regression and pretraining discussions.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies encoder freezing and documents new baseline corpus sizes, context limits, generation settings and cost/throughput estimates. It removes the direct dataset-access link and the statement that Arch2Vec/CATE encodings feed an MLP. Appendix C's code link and default hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and Section 2's novelty positioning remain: general regression from textual code across domains, contrasted with specialized feature engineering and graph methods. Citation reordering, shortened bibliography entries and the De Micheli author correction are editorial changes.

P1.justification: v2 tightens introductory and methodological prose, updates affiliations, adds an impact statement and reorganizes experimental subsections. The pretraining discussion moves into Appendix A, but most existing prose and the overall argument are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout, extensively rearranging figures and tables. v2 adds the ICL plot, relocates pretraining plots to the appendix and stacks the former side-by-side code example vertically in Figure 2, while its caption still uses left/right references.

improvement.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix A.1 strengthen the practical case for RLM by adding relevant prompted and fine-tuned language-model comparisons while preserving earlier evidence. The benefit is bounded: the decoder-only comparison changes several design factors together, new results lack uncertainty estimates, and the direct dataset link is lost. These limitations temper the added evidence without outweighing its usefulness.
